title: nf-meta-samplesheet-ops pipeline parameters
description: Generalized Nextflow adapter for pandas-style samplesheet/metadata operations (merge, drop, select, rename, dropna, drop_duplicates, filter, concat) on one or two CSV/TSV samplesheets.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Samplesheet inputs, the ordered operation chain, and where/how the result is written.

samplesheet1.description: Path to the primary CSV/TSV samplesheet.
samplesheet1.help_text: This is the samplesheet that the operation chain runs against, starting as-is and getting transformed op by op. Delimiter is auto-detected from the file extension. The first line must be a header with unique, non-repeated column names (duplicates fail the run, since every op binds columns by name). A header-only file (zero data rows) is valid; a completely empty file is not.
samplesheet1.errorMessage: samplesheet1 must be a valid file path with no spaces, ending in .csv, .tsv, or .tab, and must exist.

samplesheet2.description: Path to the second CSV/TSV samplesheet.
samplesheet2.help_text: Required only when `--ops` includes `merge` or `concat`. Always read fresh -- it is not itself transformed by earlier ops in the chain, only samplesheet1's running state is. Same header rules as samplesheet1: unique column names, header-only allowed, empty file rejected.
samplesheet2.errorMessage: samplesheet2 must be a valid file path with no spaces, ending in .csv, .tsv, or .tab, and must exist.

ops.description: Ordered, comma-separated list of operations to apply left-to-right.
ops.help_text: Allowed values: `merge`, `drop_columns`, `select_columns`, `rename`, `dropna`, `drop_duplicates`, `filter`, `concat`. Ops apply left-to-right, e.g. `merge,drop_columns,filter`. Each op may appear at most once per run -- listing one twice fails the run.
ops.errorMessage: ops must be a comma-separated list made up only of: merge, drop_columns, select_columns, rename, dropna, drop_duplicates, filter, concat.

outdir.description: Directory the output samplesheet is written to.
outdir.help_text: Created if it doesn't exist. The file is written as `<outdir>/<outname>`.

outname.help_text: The extension controls the output format: `.csv` writes comma-delimited, `.tsv`/`.tab` writes tab-delimited.

quote.description: Quote character used both when parsing input CSV/TSV and when quoting output fields.
quote.help_text: Used both to parse quoted fields in samplesheet1/samplesheet2 and to quote output fields. An output field is quoted when it contains the output delimiter, the quote character, or a newline; embedded quote characters are doubled (RFC4180-style).

drop_header.description: Omit the header row from the output samplesheet.
drop_header.help_text: Output-only: input parsing always treats the first line of samplesheet1/samplesheet2 as the header, regardless of this setting -- every op binds columns by name. When true and the result has zero rows, the output file is empty (0 bytes) rather than header-only.

merge_options.title: merge options
merge_options.description: Arguments for the 'merge' op (joins samplesheet1's running state with samplesheet2).

merge_on.description: Single shared key column present in both sheets to join on.
merge_on.help_text: Must exist in both samplesheet1's running state and samplesheet2. Keys are compared as exact strings. Repeated keys are allowed on either side: every left row is paired with every matching right row (like a SQL/pandas join), and output rows follow samplesheet1's row order.

merge_how.help_text: `inner` keeps only left rows that have at least one match in samplesheet2. `left` keeps all rows from samplesheet1's running state, blank-filling samplesheet2's columns when a row is unmatched. samplesheet2-only rows are never output.

merge_suffixes.description: Comma-separated pair of suffixes applied to overlapping non-key column names from (samplesheet1, samplesheet2) respectively.
merge_suffixes.errorMessage: merge_suffixes must be exactly two non-empty, comma-separated values.
merge_suffixes.help_text: Only columns present in both sheets (other than merge_on) are suffixed; all other names are kept as-is. The run fails if a suffixed name collides with an existing column (e.g. merging `batch` into a sheet that already has `batch_x`).

drop_columns_cols.description: Comma-separated column names to remove, for the 'drop_columns' op.
drop_columns_cols.help_text: Required by the 'drop_columns' op. Errors if a listed column doesn't exist.

select_columns_cols.description: Comma-separated column names to keep, for the 'select_columns' op -- the inverse of drop_columns.
select_columns_cols.help_text: Required by the 'select_columns' op. All columns not listed are removed. The output column order follows the order given here. Errors if a listed column doesn't exist or is listed more than once.

rename_cols.description: Comma-separated old_key=new_key pairs, for the 'rename' op, e.g. 'sample=sample_id,batch=batch_id'.
rename_cols.help_text: Column order is unchanged; only the listed names are substituted. old_key is matched against samplesheet1's actual column names (longest match wins), so old_key or new_key may themselves contain '=' -- only the outer comma is a hard separator. Errors if old_key doesn't match an existing column, or if the result would contain duplicate column names.
rename_cols.errorMessage: rename_cols must be a comma-separated list of old_key=new_key pairs.

dropna_cols.description: Comma-separated subset of columns to check for blank values, for the 'dropna' op.
dropna_cols.help_text: Defaults to checking all columns if not set. A row is dropped if any of the listed columns is blank (empty or whitespace-only). Errors if a listed column doesn't exist.

drop_duplicates_cols.description: Comma-separated subset of columns forming the dedup key, for the 'drop_duplicates' op.
drop_duplicates_cols.help_text: Defaults to all columns if not set. Values are compared column by column as exact strings. Keeps the first occurrence per key and preserves the input row order. Errors if a listed column doesn't exist.

filter_col.description: Column to test, for the 'filter' op.
filter_col.help_text: Required by the 'filter' op. Errors if the column doesn't exist, rather than silently matching nothing (or everything).

filter_op.help_text: `eq`: value equals filter_value. `ne`: value differs from filter_value. `contains`: value contains filter_value as a substring. All comparisons are case-sensitive string comparisons; a blank cell compares as the empty string.

filter_value.description: Value to compare filter_col against, for the 'filter' op.
filter_value.help_text: Required by the 'filter' op. Always compared as a string, so `1` and `1.0` are different values.
